abstraction_design.rationale: The abstractions track the real variation (cards vs team cards, per-route load functions) and stretch to new resources well; a little mapping logic is duplicated between Card producers and one helper lives in the wrong module.

findings.issue: Client islands fetch fragments by hard-coded selectors ('#results', '#move-tables', 'team-page') that are owned by server route templates; renaming the id or tag in a template silently breaks interactivity with no shared constant or error.
findings.suggestion: Define the ids/tag names once (e.g. constants in a shared module imported by both template and island), or select via data attributes documented alongside the island.

findings.issue: The isBuildRender guard (magic hostname 'gracile-static') is copy-pasted into all 7 route handlers; a new route that forgets it will fetch live API data during the build, violating the spec's no-build-time-fetch rule.
findings.suggestion: Centralize the stub-data pattern, e.g. a withRouteData(url, loader) helper or a shared stub-props convention, so the guard can't be forgotten.

findings.issue: The 'load returns null → responseInit.status = 404 → notFound template' pattern is duplicated verbatim in 4 resource routes (moves, abilities, types, pokemon).
findings.suggestion: Extract a small route factory or helper (e.g. resourceRoute(loader, template)) so 404 handling and the document title fallback live in one place.

findings.issue: The Pokémon-types→TypeBadge mapping (with label fallback) is duplicated between getTeamCards and the Pokémon route's load(); a change to how type labels resolve touches both.
findings.suggestion: Add a typeBadgesFor(pokemon, labels) helper in lib/data.ts and use it in both places (getPokemonIndex already needs similar slot-ordering logic).

findings.issue: Species-name regex duplicated: NAME_PATTERN here vs validName in app/src/lib/data.ts:416.
findings.suggestion: Export one pattern/validator (e.g. from lib/format.ts) and reuse it.

findings.issue: moveTables is a rendering helper exported from a route module but used only inside that file; a future reader will assume it's part of the route's public surface.
findings.suggestion: Move it to components/partials.ts (or make it non-exported) so route files contain only defineRoute.

findings.issue: lit is a direct dependency but never imported — the islands are vanilla custom elements. (Gracile supports vanilla CE as a first-class feature, but the declared-but-unused dep misleads readers about the stack; it may only be needed as a peer of the framework's SSR.)
findings.suggestion: Either drop lit from dependencies if the peer resolution works without it, or add a comment/package note explaining it exists for Gracile's Lit SSR pipeline.

summary: This is a well-organized, framework-idiomatic Gracile app: data access, formatting, partials and client islands each live in one clearly-scoped module, and every Pokémon card and every API URL flows through single helpers, so most fixes and data-source changes are one-file edits. The main editability risks are implicit contracts — client islands hard-coding selectors owned by server templates, and a build-render guard plus 404 boilerplate copy-pasted into all seven routes. A future maintainer adding a route or renaming an id can break things silently, which is the difference between this and an exemplary codebase.
